newsitem.title: GERMANY: German air trade slams Schipol Airport tax breaks.
newsitem.headline: German air trade slams Schipol Airport tax breaks.

text.p: Dutch tax-breaks for Schipol airport amount to unfair competition and are distorting air travel market conditions in Europe, German air industry leaders said.
Manfred Schoelch, vice-chairman of Flughafen Frankfurt Main AG (FAG), slammed tax advantages for Amsterdam and called for a level playing field between competiting European airports.

"It cannot be right that some airports enjoy national subsidies through tax-free status while other airports such as Frankfurt have to bear all their own costs," he said at a transport industry conference at Frankfurt airport.
Schoelch called on the European Commission to allow airports to continue making their own charges policy within a non-discriminating and transparent framework.
Fees at Frankfurt airport were market-orientated, acceptable to clients and allowed the airport to make a profit, he added.
Recent increases had always been in line with inflation and airlines benefitted in the end through re-investment in infrastructure, he stresssed.
Deutsche Lufthansa chairman Juergen Weber added that it was a distortion of competition if Frankfurt Airport had to pay millions for approach roads but Amsterdam received these roads free.
Lufthansa supported Frankfurt's aim of becoming the best airport and hub in Europe, he told the conference.
"For that we are ready to pay a certain price but the value for money must be right," he said.
Ludolf van Hasselt, European Commission principal administrator, said the Commission would soon make new proposals affecting airport charges.
Airports needed to charge on the basis of transparency, non-discrimination and cost relation, he said.
"A charges and fees system based on these principles ensures fair and identical market conditions for all players," he said.
Only minimal rules for airport fees would be needed and they would not change the existing working practices of airports, he added.
